sections.description: Describes the patient’s symptoms, examination, and early laboratory/imaging findings, and frames the initial clinical problem list that prompted a search for a unifying diagnosis.
subtopics: Key symptoms: 5-year progressive fatigue, exertional dyspnoea, weight loss, anorexia, bone pain/fractures
Physical findings: pallor, icterus, premature greying, knuckle hyperpigmentation, bald tongue, scoliosis, thenar atrophy, hepatosplenomegaly, reduced basal breath sounds
Initial labs: pancytopenia with low reticulocyte count, dimorphic RBCs, basophilic stippling, Cabot rings, hypersegmented neutrophils
Nutritional status: severe vitamin B12 and folate deficiency; iron overload pattern compatible with ineffective erythropoiesis
Bone marrow: trilineage haematopoiesis, erythroid hyperplasia, increased iron stores, no dysplasia/malignancy; normal cytogenetics
DAT-positive result in context of low reticulocyte response (ineffective erythropoiesis versus immune haemolysis)
Organ involvement: hepatic fibrosis/cirrhosis and steatosis on elastography; hepatosplenomegaly; pulmonary ground-glass and fibrotic/subpleural atelectatic changes on PET-CT
Additional features: osteoporosis on DXA, vitamin D deficiency, secondary hyperparathyroidism, electrolyte abnormalities; asymmetric sensorimotor axonal polyneuropathy on EMG-NCS
Problem list synthesis: cytopenias with ineffective erythropoiesis, hepatic and pulmonary fibrosis, premature ageing features, neuropathy, skeletal fragility

sections.section_title: Focused Background: Telomere Biology Disorders and PARN
sections.description: Provides targeted pathophysiology to understand how PARN-related telomere dysfunction can produce the patient’s multisystem phenotype, without a broad detour beyond what this case requires.
subtopics: Telomere function and maintenance: TERT/TERC complex, replicative senescence, tissue predilection (marrow, epithelium, hair, hepatocytes)
Clinical spectrum of TBDs: from classic dyskeratosis congenita triad to isolated organ fibrosis or marrow failure; adult-onset and incomplete penetrance
PARN biology: nuclear exoribonuclease; role in deadenylation and 3′-end maturation of TERC; impact on telomerase biogenesis

Genotype–phenotype patterns: biallelic PARN variants causing recessive DC/HH; monoallelic variants associated with pulmonary fibrosis and/or bone marrow failure (PFBMFT4); concept of haploinsufficiency
Mechanistic link to organs involved: telomere-driven stem/progenitor exhaustion in marrow (cytopenias), alveolar epithelium (IPF), and hepatocytes (hepatic fibrosis/cirrhosis)
Environmental/physiologic modifiers: nutritional deficiency and inflammatory stress unmasking TBD susceptibility; variable expressivity and somatic genetic rescue

sections.section_title: Diagnostic Reasoning: From Ineffective Erythropoiesis to a Telomere Biology Disorder
sections.description: Explains the stepwise workup and logic used to move from common causes of cytopenia and organ dysfunction to a unifying TBD diagnosis involving a monoallelic PARN variant.
subtopics: Interpreting cytopenia: low reticulocytes and marrow erythroid hyperplasia indicating ineffective erythropoiesis; reconciliation of DAT positivity with lack of reticulocytosis
Addressing reversible causes: confirmation and repletion of B12/folate; assessment for malabsorption (reduced parietal cells/chronic gastritis)
Excluding alternative hepatic and pulmonary aetiologies: negative autoimmune serologies; non-revealing infectious workup; PET-CT without malignancy/granulomatous disease
Clue aggregation: premature greying, osteoporosis/fractures, neuropathy, hepatosplenomegaly, hepatic and pulmonary fibrosis in a young adult
When to suspect TBD without classical mucocutaneous triad: disproportionate multisystem premature-ageing features and cytopenias
Genetic testing strategy: clinical exome sequencing; identification of PARN c.613T>C (p.Cys205Arg) in conserved R3H domain
Variant interpretation using ACMG/AMP: PM1 (critical domain), PM2 (rarity), PP2 (low benign missense rate), PP3 (damaging predictions) leading to VUS classification and clinical correlation
Ancillary TBD diagnostics to consider: flow-FISH telomere length measurement; family testing and segregation if feasible
Unifying hypothesis: monoallelic PARN variant conferring TBD susceptibility with organ fibrosis; B12 deficiency as a compounding stressor for marrow function
Pitfalls and pearls: incomplete penetrance; de novo variants; reliance on clinico-genetic correlation when variant remains VUS

sections.section_title: Management Strategy and Longitudinal Care in Suspected PARN-Related TBD
sections.description: Outlines acute management of identified deficiencies, organ-specific supportive care, and long-term surveillance and transplant considerations tailored to telomere syndromes.
subtopics: Immediate measures: parenteral B12 replacement protocol; folate, vitamin D, calcium; electrolyte correction; transfusion support as needed
Rehabilitation and symptom control: physiotherapy; neuropathy management; bone health optimization (fall prevention, bisphosphonate candidacy assessment)
Hepatic care: surveillance for portal hypertension and hepatocellular carcinoma; vaccination (HAV/HBV), alcohol avoidance, metabolic risk reduction
Pulmonary care: baseline and serial PFTs and HRCT as indicated; antifibrotic therapy candidacy (nintedanib/pirfenidone) in progressive IPF; infection prevention
Hematology follow-up: periodic counts and reticulocytes; monitoring for evolving marrow failure; triggers for bone marrow biopsy repetition

Transplant considerations: early referral to centers experienced with TBD; HSCT for progressive marrow failure with telomere-aware conditioning (reduced intensity) and donor selection; lung or liver transplant candidacy and multi-organ coordination
Disease-modifying options under study: androgens (danazol/nandrolone) evidence and risks; clinical trial referral
Genetic counseling: inheritance risk, family screening, reproductive options; psychosocial support and education about VUS and evolving interpretation
Preventive care and lifestyle: infection prophylaxis when indicated, avoidance of myelotoxic agents, smoking cessation, UV/skin cancer surveillance

sections.section_title: Outcomes, Prognosis, and Key Clinical Lessons
sections.description: Summarizes the patient’s short-term outcome and distills transferable insights for practice, including prognostic drivers and red flags that should trigger evaluation for TBDs.
subtopics: Case outcome: symptomatic improvement with deficiency correction; stabilized counts at 2 weeks; ongoing hepatic/pulmonary and hematologic surveillance
Prognostic considerations in PARN-related TBD: risk of progression of IPF/HF; potential evolution to marrow failure; impact of co-stressors and age
Red flags for TBD in adults: unexplained pancytopenia with low reticulocytes; premature greying/ageing signs; early-onset hepatic or pulmonary fibrosis; lack of alternative aetiology
Diagnostic best practices: integrate telomere length testing and targeted gene panels; interpret VUS in clinical context; re-evaluate variants over time
Management pearls: correct reversible stressors; anticipate transplant needs with TBD-adapted protocols; multidisciplinary follow-up
Knowledge gaps: phenotype breadth for monoallelic PARN, liver involvement prevalence, optimal timing of disease-modifying therapies
